In botany , a spadix ( pl. : spadices ) is a type of inflorescence having small flowers borne on a fleshy stem. Spadices are typical of the family Araceae , the arums or aroids. The spadix is typically surrounded by a leaf-like curved bract known as a spathe . For example, the "flower" of the well known Anthurium spp. is a typical spadix with a large colorful spathe. [ 1 ]
